heroHeadline: PENTAGON WITHDRAWS 5,000 TROOPS FROM GERMANY; TRUMP THREATENS ITALY AND SPAIN; RUTTE: 'EUROPEANS HAVE GOTTEN THE MESSAGE' AT YEREVAN EPC SUMMIT
heroSubtitle: The NATO-US rift entered a concrete operational phase in the first week of May 2026: on May 1, the Pentagon confirmed ~5,000 US troops would be withdrawn from Germany over 12 months — the first direct military drawdown linked to the Iran war burden-sharing dispute — with Trump threatening deeper cuts from Italy and Spain. NATO sought 'urgent clarification,' Germany requested details, and Poland offered to host transferred troops. TIME magazine (May 3) reported the drawdown 'has only just begun,' while Euronews sources described 'no coherent strategy' behind the announcement — SACEUR Gen. Donahue and EUCOM had minimal advance notice. SWORD 26 (15,500 troops, 6,000 US) and the Amber Shock exercise in the Suwałki Gap continued amid the political turbulence — the military alliance demonstrably functional as the political relationship deteriorates. On May 4, at the European Political Community summit in Yerevan, Armenia, NATO Secretary General Rutte declared that European allies had 'gotten the message' from Trump and confirmed multiple allies — including Montenegro, Croatia, Romania, Portugal, Greece, Italy, Britain, France, and Germany — were implementing US base access requests and pre-positioning naval assets near the Gulf. Rutte met bilaterally with UK PM Starmer and French President Macron. Upcoming: Helsingborg NATO Foreign Ministers meeting (May 21–22); Ankara Summit (July 7–8).
